author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: this is a workspace-canonical semantic-contract design call, not a contacts-server-local doc fix.

## The actual gap

RFC 8620 §5.3 (lines 1895-1930 of rfc8620.txt) is explicit: PatchObject keys are RFC 6901 JSON Pointers with an implicit leading '/'. The semantics are:
- 'addressBookIds/ab1' = navigate into addressBookIds, replace/delete the ab1 leaf
- null at a leaf = remove that property
- intermediate paths MUST already exist on the object
- pointers MUST NOT reference inside arrays

The workspace reference `MemoryBackend` impls call `jmap_server::json_merge_patch` (RFC 7396 Merge Patch). RFC 7396 treats 'addressBookIds/ab1' as a literal top-level field name. The two semantics DIVERGE for any patch with '/' in a key.

## Workspace scope

This is NOT contacts-server-local. Every extension-server's update_object trait doc has the same gap (mail-server is canonical; chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing/metadata all sibling). JMAP-510h.23 catches the same issue in filenode-server with a slightly different framing (silent no-op + bogus top-level field name).

## What the workspace has already done implicitly

Three recent commits show the workspace partially recognising the gap and handling it at the handler routing level, not at the backend semantics level:
- d8507ea (tasks-server, 2026-05-14): per-user routing splits keys on '/' before checking is_per_user_property — 'keywords/done' now routes correctly. Backend still gets the full PatchObject and still applies RFC 7396.
- b5662ac (calendars-server, 2026-05-15): same pattern for CalendarEvent/set.
- c8df9fe (filenode-server, 2026-05-14): cycle check via PatchObject not raw Value, anticipates 'a PatchObject deserializer that normalises path-form keys'.

None of these address the trait-doc gap or the actual backend semantics.

## Three options

**(a) Document trait as RFC 7396, fix handler to flatten pointer keys.**
- Trait doc: 'patch is an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch. Handler is responsible for converting RFC 8620 §5.3 JSON-Pointer-keyed wire values into merge-patch shape.'
- Handler work: implement a non-trivial pointer-to-merge-patch conversion (RFC 6901 escape decoding, intermediate-object creation, array-replacement, §5.3 restriction enforcement).
- Cost: a workspace-wide helper in jmap-server, called by every handler before backend dispatch. Backend trait surface unchanged.

**(b) Document trait as RFC 8620 §5.3 PatchObject, reshape reference backend to use a pointer-aware apply helper.**
- Trait doc: 'patch is an RFC 8620 §5.3 PatchObject. Backend MUST navigate JSON Pointer paths, treating null as leaf-removal, rejecting pointers into arrays, rejecting pointer-prefix-conflicts.'
- Backend work: replace json_merge_patch with a pointer-aware apply_jmap_patch helper in jmap-server. Reference MemoryBackend impls switch.
- Cost: foundation library API addition. Consolidates the apply_jmap_patch in contacts-server/src/card.rs that JMAP-qz9v.10 already flags as a duplicate.

**(c) Status-quo + document the workspace policy explicitly: backends apply RFC 7396 merge patch and silently misinterpret JSON Pointer keys.**
- This is what runs today. Documenting it as policy makes the silent-divergence-from-RFC-8620 a deliberate decision rather than a latent bug.
- Cost: zero code. But it violates the workspace AGENTS.md 'silent-truncation/silent-drop in any function that mutates state is a data-integrity bug class' policy (JMAP-wlip.1 precedent).

## Recommendation

**Option (b)**: it consolidates with JMAP-qz9v.10 (apply_jmap_patch duplicate), satisfies RFC 8620 §5.3 by construction, and matches the partial recognition that d8507ea + b5662ac + c8df9fe already exhibit. The cost is one foundation-library helper plus seven MemoryBackend switches; the alternative is paying the same complexity inside every handler in option (a) or accepting spec-divergence as policy in option (c).

But this is genuinely a human design call: the workspace has been drifting into (c) without explicit decision, and the human may have reasons to prefer (a) (keeps backend trait surface minimal — backends are 'just merge JSON objects' rather than 'implement RFC 6901 pointer semantics').

## Sibling beads to address in the same decision

- JMAP-qz9v.10 (contacts-server apply_jmap_patch duplicate)
- JMAP-510h.23 (filenode-server canonical version of this finding)
- JMAP-qz9v.20 (the existing 'what is good' bead on json_merge_patch foundation seam — closes under option (b), stays open under (a)/(c))
- Any mail-server-canonical review epic finding in this family
